children: Chinese President Xi Jinping is coming to America to visit U.S. President Donald Trump. Cars will be on the agenda.

The two men will dine at the White House on Thursday evening with many U.S. business leaders in attendance, including General Motors CEO Mary Barra and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, according to Reuters. GM and Tesla didn't immediately respond to a request for comment about the dinner.

That almost guarantees discussions about the global car business. The U.S. is stable, with GM, Ford Motor, and Tesla generating stable profits. The Chinese business isn't. Overcapacity has led to weak profits, with Chinese auto makers looking to export markets to soak up excess production.

Investors are a little nervous that China would like to export cars to the U.S. Recently, Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D., Mich.) suggested that Trump would allow Chinese cars to be sold in the States. That would shift China's capacity problems here.
Musk and Barra are likely to support continued tariffs on Chinese imports.

They would also like to see the Chinese industry restructure. Tesla's largest, most productive plant is located in China, and the country accounts for roughly 20% of its total sales. GM has significant business in China, too, though it has posted losses recently. GM recognized a $316 million equity loss from Chinese operations in 2025. That was an improvement from a 2024 loss of $4.4 billion.

Both stocks were relatively quiet ahead of the dinner. Tesla shares were up 0.9% in early trading, at $382.36, while the S&P 500 was down 0.4% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down about 0.2%. GM stock was down 0.6%, at $83.
